items.title: For a finite length module over a local ring the determinant is one-dimensional and generated by the symbol of any spanning admissible sequence
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)

items.difficulty_reason: For a local ring R with residue field kappa and a finite length R-module M, the lemma asserts that det_kappa(M) is a one-dimensional kappa-vector space and is generated by the symbol [f_1,...,f_l] of any admissible sequence with <f_1,...,f_l> = M (statement lines 15849-15857). The proof does not recompute the relations: that det_kappa(M) has dimension at most one and is generated by the symbol of a spanning admissible sequence is quoted from Lemma labelled lemma-dimension-at-most-one together with its proof (proof lines 15859-15862), and the new content is nonvanishing, proved by induction on the length l. The induction step picks a nonzero f with m f = 0 and constructs a surjection psi from det_kappa(M) onto det_kappa(M/<f>) by an explicit rule on symbols: send [e_1,...,e_l] to zero if f is not in <e_1,...,e_l>, and otherwise choose the minimal i with f in <e_1,...,e_i>, write e_i = lambda f + x with lambda a unit, and map to (-1)^i lambda-bar times the symbol with the i-th entry deleted (proof lines 15863-15885). The bulk is checking that this rule kills each of the three families of admissible relations: type (a) (proof lines 15887-15897), type (b) with the nontrivial subcase i = a resolved by the rewrite e'_a = lambda^{-1}(mu f + y - x) (proof lines 15899-15965), and type (c) split into four cases according to the position of i relative to a (proof lines 15967-16060); surjectivity then follows by lifting an admissible sequence from M/<f> (proof lines 16062-16066). Carrying the induction through every relation family with the correct signs and indices is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
